CHROMIUM: devfreq: rockchip: Add clk-rk3288-dmc driver The driver provides an API to change the frequency of the DDR PLL. DDR memory must not be accessed during a DDR frequency change. To achieve this the following steps are involved: - pause all CPUs except the primary one - disable interrupts - disable MMU - execute code to change the DPLL rate and update controller parameters from SRAM - resume execution from DDR, re-enable MMU, interrupts and CPUs To avoid a janky display DDR frequency changes need to be synchronized with display VBLANK events. The dmc_sync driver is used for this purpose. Before a frequency change we obtain a deadline from dmc_sync by which the rate change needs to be completed. During the steps before the actual rate change the driver repeatedly performs checks and aborts the operation if the deadline was exceeded. This code is mostly copied from the downstream Chrome OS 3.14 tree with the following changes: - don't register the DMC clock with the Common Clock Framework (CCF). store a pointer to the instance struct in a static global, since it isn't associated with a clk object - delete now unused CCF callbacks - rk3288_dmcclk_round_rate() - adapted API - use fixed 24 MHz rate for IO_XIN24M - rk3288_dmcclk_set_rate() - adapted API - round requested rate to available rate (formerly done by CCF) - do nothing if rate hasn't changed - store current frequency in existing dmc->cur_freq - use 'service_bus' instead of 'noc' to be in line with the DT and the TRM - use 'ret' macro in call_with_mmu_disabled (see 6ebbf2ce437b "ARM: convert all "mov.* pc, reg" to "bx reg" for ARMv6+" for reference) - replaced BSYM() with badr macro (see 14327c662822 "ARM: replace BSYM() with badr assembly macro") - moved from drivers/clk/rockchip/ to drivers/devfreq/rockchip/ BUG=chromium:941638 TEST=with CL:1574236 and CONFIG_ARM_RK3288_DMC_DEVFREQ=y on veyron: setting of min/max_freq in /sys/class/devfreq/devfreqN is reflected in clock 'dpll_ddr' (see /sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary) Change-Id: I5368dae651e50dbf9bffb8409f46ea41932f59d3 Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1574234 Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: devfreq: Add rk3288 DMC driver This adds a devfreq driver for the DMC clock of the Rockchip rk3288. It sets the DDR controller frequency and voltage based on the hardware usage counters. For a DDR frequency change the driver takes care of the following: - prevent CPU hotplug during the frequency change - sync DDR frequency changes with display VBLANKs - bump the CPU frequency to ensure the CPU is running fast enough to complete the frequency change within the current VBLANK pulse. Block CPU frequency changes until the DDR frequency has been adjusted. The frequency change is aborted if the CPU can't run fast enough (e.g. because it is thermally throttled). - adjust regulator voltage if needed - set the new DMC clock rate The bulk of the frequency change is performed in the context of a high priority workqueue to ensure it is finished ASAP. This code is mostly copied from the downstream Chrome OS 3.14 tree with the following changes: - removed dmc_clk field from struct rk3288_dmcfreq - rk3288_dmcfreq_work() - call rk3288_dmcclk_set_rate() instead of clk_set_rate() - adapted retry handling - renamed variable rate to prev_rate - fixed bogus error check - made checks for rate increase/decrease more readable - removed DMC clock lookup from rk3288_dmcfreq_probe() - deleted rk3288_dmc_rates to have devfreq populate the .freq_table with the OPPs of the parent device - save the current voltage when setting it, instead of doing weird OPP acrobatics in rk3288_dmcfreq_target() - use a devfreq_cooling device instead of doing things manually - upstream renamed of_init_opp_table() to dev_pm_opp_of_add_table() - removed rcu_read_lock/unlock() around OPP calls and dev_pm_opp_put() calls when an OPP isn't used anymore (see 8a31d9d9429 "PM / OPP: Update OPP users to put reference") - changed polling interval from 200ms to 100ms, now that we don't hold the global clock lock during frequency changes - normalized some checks for errors in a voltage change - renamed noc to service_bus to match the TRM and the DT BUG=chromium:941638 TEST=on veyron with CONFIG_ARM_RK3288_DMC_DEVFREQ=y: start browser in guest mode and wait 5s grep dpll_ddr /sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary => dpll_ddr ... 200000000 open webgl 'aquarium' demo with 1000 fishes grep dpll_ddr /sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary => dpll_ddr ... 532000000 Change-Id: I7c8660181d41e733d88d3d4d2173678b483970cf Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1574235 Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drivers: net: SFE port to Linux-4.14 Linux kernel does not guarantee API compatibility across releases. SFE relies upon multiple Linux kernel facilities, such as generic netlink, netfilter, and conntrack. A number of these module APIs have evolved during the ~3 year time period since SFE was originally imported into Linux-3.18. These changes port the Linux-3.18 SFE code to Linux-4.14. Linux-4.0 eliminated the return code from generic netlink message finalization because that API could never return an error. SFE adaptation is to eliminate checking for return error code. biod: Add retries for device init operations This CL adds an additional retry to the critical fingerprint MCU probing operations, which take place during biod startup. The error can be reproduced using the stress tester in CL:1556384 (patchset 11). The same stress tester was used to verify that this solution. Reads and ioctls to the fingerprint MCU (/dev/cros_fp) have been shown to occasionally fail with ETIMEDOUT. If a read/cmd fails during the startup of biod, it may be led to believe that the system does not have a fingerprint sensor/mcu. This renders the fingerprint system inoperable until a reboot is issued. Failures during the runtime of biod are less critical, since the operation can be reattempted by the user. This patchset does not cover the entire startup process. A followup patchset will enable retries for the remaining startup operations.
